resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (resale housing inspection)
resale_co.lead_time: No minimum lead time published; an expedited inspection within 5 days of the request costs $200.
requirements: Carbon monoxide detector in the hallway outside the bedrooms, within 10 feet of each bedroom (one per hallway on each bedroom floor)
Fire extinguisher 2A 10 BC mounted no higher than 5 feet, within 10 feet of the kitchen
All windows open, close and lock; screens on windows and patio doors without rips
Outlets grounded; GFCI outlets working near water sources
Toilets flush properly, no leaks under sinks
Oven and stove working with an anti-tilt bracket
Overflow pipe on the water heater
Heater certification and chimney certification before the CO is issued
Railings for 4 or more steps or 30 inches and above
House number on the home; exterior maintained
No active, open or unpaid permits

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Housing Inspection Request (listed as Residential CO Application on the Licenses & Inspections page) and return it to Caitlyn Bryant or Anthony Trappanese by email to HousingInspection@twp.burlington.nj.us or fax 609-239-6293. Licenses & Inspections is at 851 Old York Road.

evidence.quote: Housing/Rental/Apartment Inspections are to provide minimum, reasonable standards before the occupancy of a home/apartment
Certificate of Occupancy is valid for 60 days after date of issuance.
Heater certifications and Chimney certifications are required on all Single Family, Townhouses, and Condo Re-sale and Rental properties, prior to issuance of Certificate of Occupancy.
RETURN FORM TO : Caitlyn Bryant or Anthony Trappanese FAX: 609-239-6293 OR EMAIL: HousingInspection@twp.burlington.nj.us
THIS IS NOT A COMPLETE LIST OF EVERYTHING THAT IS CHECKED DURING AN INSPECTION, BUT THE MOST COMMON ITEMS THAT PREVENT A C.C.O. TO BE ISSUED.
Anthony Trappanese, Housing Inspector/Zoning Officer/Property Maintenance Inspector Office Hours: Monday-Friday 8:00A.M.-4:00P.M. (609)239-5845 atrappanese@twp.burlington.nj.us

resale_co.notes: Burlington Township's own site does not quote the ordinance, but its Licenses & Inspections page, fee sheet (Rental & Resale Inspection Fees, updated 10/2023) and Housing Inspection Request cover resale inspections and the resulting certificate of occupancy. If a re-inspection is not done within 60 days of the original inspection, a new inspection and fee are required; this also applies if the CO expires before closing, and heater and chimney certifications expire with the CO. Anthony Trappanese's direct email is atrappanese@twp.burlington.nj.us. The staff directory lists Caitlyn Bryant at (609) 239-5847 while the Licenses & Inspections page lists her at (609)239-5846; the department's main line is (609) 239-5847. Township ordinances are on ecode360 (BU2696), which could not be opened. Note: the ecode360 lead in the Watchdog leads (BU2898) is Burlington City's code, not the township's.

requirements: Carbon monoxide detectors in the bedroom hallway, within 10 feet of each bedroom
Fire extinguisher 2A 10 BC mounted in the kitchen no more than 5 feet above the floor (still listed on the township page and 2018 items sheet)

fire_cert.notes: The fire code enforcing agency for Burlington Township is the fire district (Burlington Township Fire Department, Bureau of Fire Prevention, 1601 Burlington Bypass). The district's own page names Fire Official Matthew Tomaszewski (609-239-5850, mtomaszewski@btfd.org), while the DCA directory (survey 7/22/2026) still lists Ashley L Johnson (ajohnson@btfd.org); the district page is used as more current. The DCA directory lists 'Burlington Twp Inspections' at 851 Old York Rd, (609) 239-5847 for smoke detector compliance, and the township page says its housing inspector checks smoke, CO and extinguisher, so the resale smoke/CO check appears to be done in the township housing inspection with no separate fire district fee. This is inferred from those two sources; no page states it in one sentence.
